name: Long-Term Resident (LTR) Visa (Board of Investment)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires investment in Thailand of at least USD 500,000 in the applicant's own name, in Thai government bonds (5+ years' remaining maturity), direct investment in a Thai-registered company, or qualifying Thai property -- confirmed directly per BOI Announcement No. Por 3/2568. No income figure is required under this category; wealth alone is the test.
requirements.fix_path: Structure a qualifying USD 500,000 investment in Thailand.

requirements.blocker_text: Alternatively, a minimum of USD 1,000,000 in total global net assets is accepted without the separate Thailand-investment requirement -- this global-assets threshold rests on strong tier-3 cross-corroboration rather than the same directly-fetched BOI announcement confirmed for the USD 500,000 Thailand-investment pathway.
requirements.fix_path: Document at least USD 1,000,000 in total global net assets.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires the applicant to be at least 50 years old.

Requires annual pension or passive income (excluding salary or director fees) of at least USD 80,000/year, or at least USD 40,000/year combined with an investment of at least USD 250,000 in Thai government bonds, direct investment, or property.
requirements.fix_path: Document qualifying passive/pension income at or above the applicable threshold, combined with the reduced-income investment option if income alone falls short.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires an established relationship with a foreign-registered employer that is publicly listed, has combined revenue of at least USD 50 million over the past 3 years, or employs at least 150 staff -- a real, current standard replacing the programme's original 2022 'top-500-company' language, per one specialist source not independently confirmed against a primary BOI page in this research pass.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm the foreign employer meets the current revenue/listing/headcount standard.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires income of at least USD 80,000/year over the past 2 years, plus at least 5 years of relevant professional experience. Unlike the Wealthy Global Citizen and Wealthy Pensioner categories, this category does NOT receive the foreign-sourced-income tax exemption.
requirements.fix_path: Document the qualifying income history and professional experience.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires income of at least USD 80,000/year in a BOI-targeted sector (advanced manufacturing, digital/AI, biomedical, smart electronics, aviation, and similar), reduced to USD 40,000/year for applicants with a master's degree or higher in a relevant field, employed by a qualifying business entity, higher-education institution, research centre, or Thai government agency.
requirements.fix_path: Document income meeting the applicable threshold, reduced if holding a qualifying master's degree or higher.

outcome_override.duration_length: 10 years (two consecutive 5-year periods), renewable, not exceeding the underlying contract term

evidence_required.document: Investment, asset, or income documentation matching the applicable category
Health insurance covering at least USD 50,000 inpatient (or a qualifying deposit/social-security alternative)
BOI application processed via the One Stop Service Center (TIESC), official target 20 business days though 2-4 months is more typical in practice

outcome.duration_length: 10 years (two consecutive 5-year periods), renewable, with full BOI eligibility reassessment at the 5-year renewal point
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: annual address reporting only, instead of the standard 90-day reporting cycle other long-stay visas require

sources.title: Board of Investment (ltr.boi.go.th) -- official English-translation PDF of Announcement of the Office of the Board of Investment No. Por 3/2568, confirming the Wealthy Global Citizen USD 500,000 Thailand-investment threshold directly

notes: Four genuinely distinct qualifying groups, correctly modeled as OR-logic per this schema's core design decision, directly mirroring the programme's own official structure (Ministry of Interior/BOI joint measure, applications accepted since 1 September 2022). SOURCING NOTE: one requirement per group is directly tier-1 sourced from a fetched BOI announcement PDF (the Wealthy Global Citizen investment threshold); the remaining figures rest on strong, mutually-consistent cross-corroboration across 5+ independent specialist sources rather than additional direct government fetches -- flagged honestly rather than uniformly claimed as tier-1. As a consequence, the Wealthy Pensioner and Highly Skilled Professional groups currently have no hard:true gate at all (their only requirements are marked hard:false pending a tier-1 upgrade), while Wealthy Global Citizen and Work-from-Thailand Professional each retain at least one hard:true requirement -- an honest reflection of this build's sourcing state rather than a claim that those two groups are easier to qualify for in practice; a follow-up session fetching the BOI's own category-specific announcement pages (parallel to the Wealthy Global Citizen PDF already fetched) would likely resolve this cleanly, since the figures themselves are not seriously in dispute across sources checked. STRUCTURAL FINDING, a real and consequential distinction confirmed across multiple sources: LTR years do NOT count toward Thai Permanent Residency at all -- an LTR holder wanting a PR pathway needs to separately pursue the retirement (O-A) or employment-based PR tracks documented on th_permanent_residence, since the two systems (BOI's LTR programme and the Immigration Bureau's PR programme) are administratively and legally independent of each other despite both offering long-term status. The Highly Skilled Professional group's outcome_override exists because it alone requires and grants full work rights (a mandatory digital work permit, plus the flat 17% income-tax rate on employment income) rather than the passive-income tax exemption the other three categories receive -- a genuine difference in what the route grants, not merely in the qualifying test, justifying the override per this schema's design intent. BOI publishes real, current approval statistics: 10,473 total LTR visas issued since the September 2022 launch through June 2026, with Wealthy Pensioners consistently the largest applicant group (accounting for 70% of the programme's growth in its strongest month on record) -- a genuine usage-scale finding worth surfacing, in contrast to Russia's comparable but far lower-uptake investor-visa programme documented elsewhere in this dataset.
